name: Xue Delong
current_role: Chairman (per company site) and largest individual shareholder (~16.19% as of Mar 2026) of ZYNP Corporation (SZSE: 002448), Mengzhou, Henan
profile: Xue Delong built ZYNP Corporation (Zhongyuan Neipei), a former state-owned piston/cylinder-liner maker founded in 1958 in Henan, into a Shenzhen-listed company (IPO July 2010). The company calls itself the world's largest cylinder-liner producer. He holds about 16% of its shares.
interesting_fact: ZYNP says its 'Heyang' brand cylinder liners hold over 15% of the international market and about 45% of China's domestic market; the company dates back to March 1958.
deep_cut_fact: The company profile credits him personally with the 'Three Development Strategies' plan to turn ZYNP into an 'international and world-class' enterprise group.
notes: Some 2026 executive databases list Xue Yahui (b. 1981) as chairman & GM, so Xue Delong may have handed over the chair; check the latest SZSE/cninfo filings. Company phone 0086-391-8190221 is published on its site. No English press presence; Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Prava Ranjan Patnaik
current_role: Managing Director, Falcon Marine Exports Ltd (per company-registry aggregators, DIN 00417793); also director of Falcon Holdings, Falcon Finance and Falcon Real Estate
profile: Prava Ranjan Patnaik is listed as managing director of Falcon Marine Exports, a Bhubaneswar, Odisha-based shrimp/seafood exporter, and of other Falcon Group companies. The group was founded in 1985 by Tara Ranjan Patnaik and grew into one of India's largest shrimp exporters, using thousands of contract farms. It later added real estate and other businesses.
interesting_fact: Falcon Marine Exports' promoters (the Patnaik family) appeared in the 2024 Hurun India Rich List at about Rs 4,900 crore. The company won MPEDA's award as India's highest-value seafood exporter over 15 years (2017).
notes: Almost all press covers group founder Tara Ranjan Patnaik and his son Parthajeet; Prava's exact relationship to them (likely a family member) is not confirmed in sources found. Very low public profile. No official website or published contact found; outreach via Falcon Group HQ (Falcon House, Bhubaneswar) or the Tara/Parthajeet Patnaik side is likely the best route.

name: Venkat Ramaswamy
current_role: Vice Chairman, Edelweiss Group (Edelweiss Financial Services); heads the alternatives business (Edelweiss Alternatives / EAAA)
profile: Venkatchalam 'Venkat' Arakoni Ramaswamy co-founded Edelweiss with Rashesh Shah in 1995. The two had been colleagues at ICICI. Edelweiss grew into a diversified Indian financial-services group, and he is now vice chairman. He leads its alternatives arm, a major private-credit and infrastructure investor in India.
interesting_fact: The alternatives arm he leads raised INR 8,000 crore for its Infrastructure Yield Plus II fund, which buys operating roads and renewable-energy assets. A 2026 report said it was in talks for a third fund of about $1bn+. That is directly relevant to the energy/infrastructure theme.
deep_cut_fact: Edelweiss started in 1995 as a three-person startup that Rashesh Shah launched with his ICICI colleague Venkat Ramaswamy after both quit their jobs.
notes: Lower media profile than co-founder Rashesh Shah, but quoted in fund-raise announcements and speaks at CFA Society India events. Edelweiss's investor-services page lists the company secretary (Tarun Khurana) at Edelweiss House, Kalina, Mumbai. No press email was confirmed (site blocked automated fetch). Good energy-transition/infra-fund angle.

name: Aaron Cowen
current_role: Founder, CIO and Managing Partner, Suvretta Capital Management (New York); director of Veradermics and Benitec Biopharma
profile: Aaron Cowen is a hedge-fund manager who founded Suvretta Capital Management in 2011-12 after stints at Lehman Brothers, Baupost, Karsch Capital, SAC Capital (CIO) and Soros. Suvretta runs generalist and healthcare/biotech long-short funds (the Averill funds). He holds large stakes in and sits on the boards of several biotechs, including Veradermics, Benitec and ProKidney.
interesting_fact: By mid-2023 Suvretta's biotech/healthcare-focused Averill funds had grown to double the size of its flagship generalist funds.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Seth Klarman's Baupost Group in 1997 as an analyst for two years after starting as an associate at Lehman Brothers. He then spent 6+ years as a managing director at Karsch Capital before becoming SAC's CIO.
notes: Low-profile hedge-fund manager. No published press contact or personal social accounts found; Suvretta has no informative public website. Best route is likely via the IR/press contacts of portfolio companies where he is a director (e.g. Veradermics, Benitec). Biotech focus, so limited fit with an energy/data-center theme.

name: Aaron Jagdfeld
current_role: President and CEO, Generac Holdings (NYSE: GNRC), Waukesha, Wisconsin; director, Hillman Solutions
profile: Jagdfeld joined Generac in its finance department in the mid-1990s and became CFO in 2002. As CFO he helped sell the company to CCMP for about $2bn in 2006. He became CEO in 2008 at 36 and took Generac public in 2010. He has turned Generac into the leading US home-standby generator maker and now a fast-growing supplier of backup power for data centers.
interesting_fact: In Q3 2026 Generac signed a long-term supply deal for backup generators for Amazon data centers, with initial deliveries of about $2.4bn in 2027-28. Jagdfeld said the data-center backlog had reached about $4.5bn.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Deloitte & Touche auditor in Milwaukee when Generac, one of the manufacturers he audited, offered him a job. Years later he said of the business: 'We don't have a company jet.'
notes: Top fit for an energy/data-center podcast: Generac is pivoting hard into data-center backup power (Amazon deal, capacity expansion). He regularly does earnings calls and trade-press interviews. Route via Generac IR/communications.

name: Mukesh Chimanlal Gandhi
profile: Co-founder, Whole-time Director and CFO of MAS Financial Services (Ahmedabad NBFC founded 1995). Died January 19, 2021, according to the company's founders page.
notes: Deceased (Oct 20, 1957 - Jan 19, 2021), source: https://mas.co.in/about/#our-founders. The surviving founder is co-founder Kamlesh Gandhi (Chairman & MD); company contact mfsl@mas.co.in is published at https://www.mas.co.in/.

name: Rajender Singh
current_role: Associated with Gawar Construction Ltd (Hisar/Gurugram, Haryana) per rich-list data; not on the company's current published board
profile: Gawar Construction is a Haryana highway, expressway, tunnel and bridge builder. It began in 1997 as a partnership, became a limited company in 2008 and is CRISIL AA-rated. It has built 12,000+ lane-km and has an order book of about Rs 16,000 crore. It sponsors the Capital Infra Trust InvIT. Rajender Singh is listed as the wealth holder, but the published board shows founders Rakesh Kumar and Ravinder Kumar.
interesting_fact: Gawar has moved 12 completed hybrid-annuity (HAM) road SPVs into an InvIT it sponsors (Capital Infra Trust). It says 12 of its projects earned early-completion bonuses in five years.
notes: Identity uncertain: the company site does not mention a Rajender Singh. He may be the family patriarch behind founders Rakesh Kumar and Ravinder Kumar, but this is unconfirmed; verify before outreach. Approach via the company's contact page. The only published email is hr@gawar.in (careers), which is not suitable. The web-search budget ran out during this lane, so research was limited.

name: Zhu Zhangjin
current_role: President (总裁) of Kasen Group / Kasen International Holdings (HKEX: 0496), Haining, Zhejiang; chairman of its Cambodian special economic zone
profile: Zhu Zhangjin built Kasen from a small tannery (1988) into a leather and sofa exporter, listed in Hong Kong in 2005. The group expanded into property and resorts in Hainan and Changbaishan. Since 2019 Kasen has repositioned as a Belt-and-Road special-economic-zone operator in Cambodia and an international power developer. It builds thermal, solar, hydro and wind projects in Mongolia, Cambodia and Zimbabwe.
interesting_fact: Kasen now develops power projects (coal, solar, hydro, wind, district heating) in Mongolia, Cambodia and Zimbabwe with Chinese state builders. It also runs the 15,000-mu Koh Kong Zhejiang Special Economic Zone in Cambodia, launched 2022-23.
deep_cut_fact: Kasen began in 1988 as the Qingyun Huafeng tannery, making pigskin and sheepskin garment leather. By 2001 its leather sofas were exported to Europe and the US and, per the company, 'placed in the White House'.
notes: Listed (Wikipedia) among Zhejiang delegates to the National People's Congress. He accompanied President Hu Jintao on a 2008 state visit to the Americas. Strong energy/infrastructure angle (overseas power plants). Chinese-language outreach advised; the HK email is the listed company's IR mailbox (via IMS).

name: Kevin Scott Kirby
current_role: Co-founder and ~13% shareholder of Abacus Global Management (Nasdaq: ABX), Orlando, Florida; former President after the 2023 SPAC listing
profile: K. Scott Kirby co-founded Abacus Settlements in 2004 with Sean McNealy and Matthew Ganovsky, and served as a managing partner building the life-settlements market. Abacus buys and trades life-insurance policies for institutional investors. It went public via a SPAC merger in 2023 and has since expanded into asset management. He served as President after the listing and remains one of its largest holders.
interesting_fact: Abacus's 2023 merger proxy says its three managing partners co-founded the firm in 2004 and 'helped build the institutional and broker market for the entire industry' of life settlements.
deep_cut_fact: He is a University of Central Florida business-management graduate (BSBA) and has held a Florida life and annuity license since 2006.
notes: The April 2026 proxy lists him only as a 5%+ holder (13.1%), not among executive officers, so he may have stepped back from day-to-day management. Low public profile. Route via Abacus PR. Weak fit for an energy/data-center theme.

name: Steven A J Salamon
current_role: Co-founder and Portfolio Manager, Rosalind Advisors (life-sciences investment manager, Toronto); director of Delcath Systems since May 2020
profile: Steven Salamon co-founded Rosalind Advisors in 2006. The life-sciences fund's Rosalind Master Fund and Rosalind Opportunities Fund are large holders in small-cap biotech and medtech. He was earlier an equity analyst at HSBC Securities and RBC Capital Markets. He joined Delcath's board under a board-appointment agreement with the Rosalind funds.
interesting_fact: Before finance he was a product engineer at Chrysler. He holds a University of Toronto Engineering Physics degree and an Ivey MBA.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a product engineer at Chrysler Corporation before his Ivey MBA, then moved to equity research at RBC Dominion Securities and HSBC before co-founding Rosalind in 2006.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Engineering background (Chrysler, engineering physics) could be a hook. Weak fit with an energy/data-center theme. Route via Delcath IR or Rosalind Advisors.

name: Ryan Berry
current_role: Partner and Chief Marketing & Strategy Officer, Ares Management Corporation (NYSE: ARES), Los Angeles (in role since Jan 2018; 2026 proxy notes he was no longer an executive officer at end-2025)
profile: Ryan Berry joined Ares in 2005 as a private-equity investment professional after working as a UBS investment-banking analyst in Los Angeles. As Chief Marketing & Strategy Officer he led Ares' global expansion: asset-manager acquisitions, strategic partnerships, distribution and the 2014 IPO. He is one of the 'Holdco Members' who control Ares' general partner and holds a substantial stake in the firm.
interesting_fact: He is one of six 'Holdco Members', alongside Ares co-founders Arougheti, Kaplan, Ressler and Rosenthal plus Kipp deVeer, who control Ares Management's general partner.
deep_cut_fact: He has two degrees from Western University in Canada: a B.A. with distinction in Business Administration from the Ivey Business School and a B.A. in Cross Disciplinary Studies from Huron University College.

public_contacts.value: Carl Drake, Partner/Senior Advisor to Public Markets IR and Corporate Communications, cdrake@ares.com

notes: The 2026 proxy says he was an NEO for 2025 'despite not being an executive officer at the end of 2025', so his role may have changed; verify before outreach. Ares is a big infrastructure, digital-infrastructure and energy investor, so there is a podcast angle. Low personal media profile; route via Ares corporate communications.
